status_summary: On 2025-03-21 EOIR reinstated its 2019 policy on status dockets (PM 25-27), and on 2025-04-18 its Acting Director issued PM 25-29, rescinding the 2021 memo on administrative closure and stating that no statute authorizes it, while noting the 2024 rule stayed binding until rescinded or vacated. On 2026-06-22 the Northern District of Texas entered a consent judgment in Texas v. DOJ declaring the 2024 EOIR docket rule in excess of statutory authority and contrary to law, vacating it, permanently enjoining its enforcement and enjoining future regulations allowing administrative closure without express statutory authorization, with the parties waiving appeal. On 2026-08-21 the court denied a motion by three cities and a legal services group to intervene, finding they lacked standing; they appealed to the Fifth Circuit (No. 26-10794), which per the federal respondents' brief denied a stay, and their stay application to the Supreme Court (No. 26A500, filed 2026-10-09) had no order as of the docket read on 2026-10-28. The actions limit immigration judges' closure authority; ICE's own use of termination and closure motions was not shown to have changed by a written policy.

timeline.event: EOIR Acting Director issued PM 25-29, effective the same day, cancelling Director's Memorandum 22-03 (2021) on administrative closure, stating that no statute authorizes administrative closure by EOIR adjudicators and that EOIR would not defend the 2024 docket management rule against legal challenge, while noting the rule remained binding until rescinded, superseded, enjoined, vacated or found unlawful.

In Texas v. DOJ (N.D. Tex., No. 7:26-cv-00070-O) the court enters an Order and Final Judgment (ECF 5) on the parties' joint motion (ECF 3) the same day the complaint was filed: it declares the 2024 EOIR docket management rule (89 FR 46742) in excess of statutory authority and contrary to law and declares that no statute authorizes immigration judges to close cases indefinitely; it permanently enjoins enforcement of the rule, enjoins future regulations allowing administrative closure without express statutory authorization, vacates the rule, and records the parties' waiver of appeal.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court, N.D. Tex. (CourtListener RECAP)

title: End administrative closure and termination of pending immigration cases
uncertainties: The Mandate's pages 141 and 152 address ICE's use of closure and termination, while the actions found are by EOIR and a court, which control the immigration judge's authority; the record is therefore a partial match. The Order and Final Judgment (ECF 5) and the 2026-08-21 Opinion and Order (ECF 23) were opened and read on court copies (storage.courtlistener.com and law.justia.com), so the vacatur, the injunctions on enforcement and on future closure rules without express statutory authority, and the appeal waiver are read from the judgment itself. The text of ECF 5 as read did not show the signing judge's name; the name comes from ECF 23 and the case-tracking docket. ECF 23 does not report an appeal. The appeal is Fifth Circuit No. 26-10794, as shown on the Supreme Court docket for No. 26A500 read on supremecourt.gov on 2026-10-26: the City of Baltimore, Columbus, New Haven and Centro Legal de la Raza applied on 2026-10-09 for a stay, a response was requested on 2026-10-15, the federal respondents and Texas responded on 2026-10-22, the applicants replied on 2026-10-23, and no order had issued as of 2026-10-26. The Fifth Circuit's denial of a stay is reported by SCOTUSblog (2026-10-15) without a date or order number, and its order was not opened (no ca5.uscourts.gov order surfaced in search); a reported district court stay denial rests on an external retrieval and was not opened. A September 2026 advocacy advisory first reported the appeal; it is a lead only and is not cited as a source. PM 25-29 was not re-read in this pass. The 2026 BIA interim final rule does not change closure rules per the portion read earlier; a Federal Register search of EOIR rules since 2025-01-20 found no rule on administrative closure or termination. PM 25-27 is cited from the advisory only. The EOIR policy memorandum list page failed to load earlier, so other memos since 2025-01-20 may exist. Whether the Attorney General acted was not found. The vacatur follows a suit by Texas that DOJ did not defend. On 2026-10-28 the federal respondents' opposition (supremecourt.gov, 2026-10-22) was read: it reports that the Fifth Circuit denied the applicants' motion to stay the consent judgment and for summary reversal of the intervention order, and that the district court denied a stay; neither order is dated in the brief, and the intervention motion is dated 2026-08-07 there. The Supreme Court docket was re-read in review on 2026-10-28 and showed no order or entry after 2026-10-23 (the page states it was created 2026-10-26).
